senses.gloss: During the night following the current day; during the evening of today.
An administrative region in southwestern France, established in 2016 by the merger of Aquitaine, Limousin, and Poitou-Charentes.
The ordinal form of the number two thousand.
An important or main item.
Hatred of, contempt for, or prejudice against men.
A choice or judgement.
A strong will; the state of being resolute.
The judicial order for a punishment to be imposed on a person convicted of a crime.
(US) A local law, passed by e.g. a city.
Something that is stated or stipulated as a condition of an agreement.
Having four legs.
A four-footed or four-legged animal.
Walking on four feet.
A current movement that attracts wide support.
(intransitive) To be current, widespread, or predominant; to have currency or prevalence.
The act of cooperating.
To make free; set at liberty; release.
To free or liberate; to set free.
to allow or cause (someone or something) to be free — see also set free, release
situated in, or pointing to, the southwest
An error.
mistake or error
A mistake; an accidental wrong action or a false statement not made deliberately.
A fault or malfunction.
defect, fault
A temporary failure; a slip.
A clumsy or embarrassing mistake.
of lower quality
Duty; responsibility.
A character or part played by a performer or actor.
(card games) Especially in games of the rummy family: a combination of playing cards which is announced or played to score points. [from late 19th c.]
A female native or inhabitant of England; a woman who is English by birth, descent or naturalisation.
Concerned with the exchange of goods for profit.
Absurd, or contrary to common sense.
Lacking sense or meaning, often to the point of boredom or annoyance.
Festive, bright, or colourful.
Emitting much light; visually dazzling; luminous, lucent, radiant.
Emitting light.
Reflecting light.
Bright, intense, or colourful.
Having a smooth, silklike, reflective (shiny) surface.
(literary, also, figuratively) Radiant, resplendent, shining.
A group of fish or a group of marine mammals such as porpoises, dolphins, or whales.
(collective) A group of donkeys.
A cattle drive or the herd being driven by it; thus, a number of cattle driven to market or new pastures.
A number of domestic animals assembled together under the watch or ownership of a keeper.
A number of birds together in a group, such as those gathered together for the purpose of migration.
A large number of insects, especially when in motion or (for bees) migrating to a new colony.
A group, especially a large group, and especially a group of attractive girls or women.
Amusement, enjoyment or pleasure.

An activity designed to give pleasure, enjoyment, diversion, amusement, or relaxation to an audience, no matter whether the audience participates passively as in watching opera or a movie, or actively as in games.
For, or relating to, recreation.
Entertainment.
The act of relaxing or the state of being relaxed; the opposite of stress or tension; the aim of recreation and leisure activities.
(in combination) Uninhibited activity.
(uncountable) Joy; happiness; great delight, especially from one's own good fortune or from another's misfortune.
Something which amuses, and serves to make time pass agreeably.
work of an engineer
measure of length
Any of the suborder Serpentes of legless reptiles with long, thin bodies and fork-shaped tongues.
A snake.
Any species of the suborder Serpentes; a snake or serpent.
Of or pertaining to the axilla or armpit.
The armpit.
(botany) The angle or point of divergence between the upper side of a branch, leaf, or petiole, and the stem or branch from which it springs.
The ship occupied by the fleet's commander (usually an admiral); it denotes this by flying his flag.
One employed to take dictation, or copy manuscripts.
a desk, usually with a cover and compartments for storing papers etc. located above the level of the writing surface rather than underneath.
The husband of one's child.
A man in the context of his own wedding; one who is going to marry or has just been married.
The state of being free from physical or psychological disease, illness, or malfunction; wellness.
That which causes merriment.
A syntactic marker.
Used as an intensifier, often ironic: indeed, really, truthfully.
The exploration and scientific study of the oceans and ocean floor.
Designed to last for a long time, said especially of food and drink
Able to resist wear or decay; lasting; enduring.
Resistant or impervious to something.
The study, and formal recording of such descents.
A craftsperson who works metal into desired forms using a hammer and other tools, sometimes heating the metal to make it more workable, especially a blacksmith.
A person who forges iron.
A person who forges metals.
Someone who plates metal.
Any of numerous arboreal birds of the families Capitonidae, Lybiidae, and Megalaimidae, within the order Piciformes.
A collection of (usually) organized information in a regular structure, usually but not necessarily in a machine-readable format accessible by a computer.
An event for public entertainment and trade, a market.
A devotional exercise of, or leading to, contemplation.
Holy meditation.
simplest or essential part or principle of anything
A part, or component of a whole
As can be supported or proven by sound logical deduction, evidence, and precedent, but without absolute certainty.
A shrill noise, especially made by a voice or bird. If made by a bird, it typically signals discomfort or anger; a yell, scream, or call.
An event or a display where fireworks are set off.
A main public road, especially a multi-lane, high-speed thoroughfare.

A highway with grade-separated crossings (rather than level crossings) and designed (and only permitted) for high-speed motor-traffic (in Europe motor vehicles with a higher speed limit than 40 km/h) running in two directions on one separate carriageway each.
A divided highway, especially one whose intersections and direct access to adjacent properties have been eliminated.
A house, often larger and more expensive than average, in the countryside or on the coast, often used as a retreat.
A Turkish garden pavilion.
A belvedere, either a type of summer-house or a roofed, detached porch-like structure, usually in a yard, park or lawn.
An open stall, often on a street, where newspapers and magazines are on sale to the public.
A small, open-air platform or enclosure for bands to play on, usually roofed.
bird in the genus Meleagris
(US, Australia, NZ, Canada, informal) A dollar (one hundred cents).
A female turkey.
(uncountable) Anything made wholly or largely of iron, especially when used for decoration.
A polite form of address for a woman or lady.
(historical) A territory of the southwest Confederate (1862–1865) and United States of America (1863–1912), with its capitals at Tucson, Prescott, and Phoenix.
A percussion instrument consisting of a metal disk that emits a loud resonant sound when struck with a soft hammer.
Finely chopped meat; minced meat.
(rare) Minced meat, mince.

(cooking) An emulsion of fat and comminuted meat (which has been subject to puréeing, grinding, sieving, chopping finely) optionally mixed with other flavour carriers and either served up alone or used as a stuffing.
A group of languages that, together with Samoyedic, make up the Uralic family, and are spoken in a broad swath from Siberia to Norway.
A small or narrow opening, gap, slit, or hole.
A short tube, usually tapering, forming the vent of a hose or pipe.
A person who wrestles.
Something prearranged or faked in order to trick someone or to advance one's own interests.
A machine or other device designed to catch (and sometimes kill) animals, either by holding them in a container, or by catching hold of part of the body.
(Britain, slang) An act designed to maliciously or dishonestly incriminate someone.

A coherent statement or set of ideas that explains observed facts or phenomena and correctly predicts new facts or phenomena not previously observed, or which sets out the laws and principles of something known or observed; a hypothesis confirmed by observation, experiment etc.
In a friendly manner; like a friend.
Uncomfortably restricted in size or space, or financially.
(figurative) Inactivity; a freezing, or state of motionlessness.
(UK, Irish, Commonwealth) A line of motor vehicles causing or the result of traffic congestion or a traffic jam.
To observe over a period of time; to notice or pay attention.
Any of various fungi, usually globose, that produce a cloud of brown dust-like spores from their mature fruiting bodies, especially in family Lycoperdaceae.
When reading out a repeating decimal, denotes where the periodic part begins.
Any of various similar-appearing birds, but usually ground-living, such as the meadowlark and titlark.
A Finno-Ugric language spoken by the Mari people.
The largest island in the Mediterranean Sea, an autonomous region of Italy, close to Africa and separated from Tunisia and Libya by the Strait of Sicily.
In a disorderly state; chaotic; disorderly.
(figurative, often lower-case) Overly complex or intricate, especially of bureaucracy.
Not in order; marked by disorder or disarray.
Naturally to demand (something) as indispensable; to need, to call for as necessary.
A felt hat in the shape of a truncated cone, having a flat top with a tassel attached.
A large city and metropolitan borough of West Yorkshire, England.
To lift, move, or collect with a scoop or as though with a scoop.
Soft and easily chewed.
Likely to crunch, especially with reference to food when it is eaten.
An amusement ride consisting of a train on a track that rises, falls, twists and turns.

A railway track on which there are steep ascents and descents, a train moving partially or fully by the force of gravity using the momentum generated when descending to travel up an ascending part of the track; especially (Britain, dated) , such a track built for fun rides at an amusement park; a type of rollercoaster.
one who rides — see also cyclist, driver
(UK) A lightweight building block made from cinders and concrete.
A bulk quantity of precious metal, usually gold or silver, assessed by weight and typically cast as ingots.
(countable) A small, compact chunk or clump.

A solid block of more or less pure metal, often but not necessarily bricklike in shape and trapezoidal in cross-section, the result of pouring out and cooling molten metal, often immediately after smelting from raw ore or alloying from constituents.
(jocular) A large book, which by implication could be used to stop a door.
A North American sport involving skills with horses, cows and other livestock.
(countable) A device with interlocking parts used for fastening things together, such as a fastener or a holder.
Something or someone that fastens.
(Hinduism) A male demon, lord of Kali Yuga and the nemesis of Kalki, tenth avatar of Vishnu.
A person who or thing that collects, or which creates or manages a collection.
To free (someone) from accusation or blame.
Courteous behaviour, especially that of men towards women.
(uncountable) The official language of Bulgaria.
(Roman god) The god of love, son of Venus; sometimes depicted as a putto (a naked, winged boy with bow and arrow). The Roman counterpart of Eros.
A person from Armenia or of Armenian descent.
The third of the Books of Moses in the Old Testament of the Bible; the third book in the Torah.
A country in East Africa and Southern Africa. Official name: Republic of Mozambique (since 1990). Capital: Maputo.
A city, the capital of Padua, Veneto.
An ugly old woman, a hag.
Tasting or smelling rancid.
One who owns shares of stock in a corporation.
Streaked, spotted, or otherwise marked with a variety of color.
In accordance with, or established by, custom or common usage.
That which is believed; accepted doctrine, especially religious doctrine; a particular set of beliefs; any summary of principles or opinions professed or adhered to.
A statement of a belief or a summary statement of a whole belief system; also (metonymically) the belief or belief system itself.
Copying of another person's ideas, text, or other creative work, and presenting it as one's own, especially without permission; plagiarizing.
A severe laminitis of a horse, caused by untreated internal inflammation in the hooves.
A disease of the digital laminae of the hoof
tendency to attract
A huge mass of ocean-floating ice which has broken off a glacier or ice shelf
Extreme shortage of food in a region.
The condition of something being scarce or deficient.
The quality or degree of being tight.
To cause or produce a scarcity in something.
An abnormal narrowing or stricture in a blood vessel or other tubular organ.
The state of being narrow.

A social system based on personal ownership of resources and personal fealty between a suzerain (lord) and a vassal (subject). Defining characteristics are direct ownership of resources, personal loyalty, and a hierarchical social structure reinforced by religion.
A wasting of body tissues, of either genetic origin or due to inadequate or defective nutrition.
An incident, action, or time period standing out by itself, but more or less connected with a complete series of events.
The act of visualizing, or something visualized.
An exclamation used in songs of praise or thanksgiving to God.
To make a short, loud, explosive noise with the vocal organs (said of animals, especially dogs).
An abrupt, high-pitched noise or utterance.
to bark with a sharp, high-pitched voice
(physics, chemistry) Lacking an affinity for water; unable to absorb or to be wetted by water.
A hard wood taken from the birch tree, typically used to make furniture.
To fasten or attach (something) with a pin.
An artist’s or photographer’s workshop or the room in which an artist works.
A studio or workshop, especially for an artist, designer, or fashion house.
A hold or way of holding, particularly with the hand.
The handle of a sword, consisting of grip, guard, and pommel, designed to facilitate use of the blade and afford protection to the hand.
A pin, or handle, of the snath (shaft) of a scythe.
A projection that one may hold onto for support, e.g. in mountain climbing.
lose blood
The system of writing Japanese using Chinese characters.
The favoring of relatives (most strictly) or also personal friends (more broadly) because of their relationship rather than because of their abilities.

A thin, often colorless or blue or straw-colored petroleum-based fuel, heavier than gasoline/petrol or naphtha but lighter than diesel, used primarily as jet fuel but also for heating and lighting in some remote or impoverished areas.
An amino acid, 2-(carbamimidoyl-methyl- amino)acetic acid, which naturally occurs in vertebrates and helps to supply energy to muscle and nerve cells.
An act of irreverence or contempt toward a god or toward something considered sacred; an impious act, utterance, view, etc.
requiring a lot of effort to do or understand
To make the characteristic cry of a sheep or (broader) a sheep or goat.
Of a sheep, goat, or calf: to make its characteristic cry; of a human, to mimic this sound.
Deceptive or false appearance; that which misleads the eye or the mind.
The details of the food to be served at a banquet; a bill of fare.
An ideology which claims that the military is the foundation of a society's security, and thereby its most important aspect.

A form of government in which the governing body has absolute, or almost absolute, control. Typically this control is maintained by force, and little heed is paid to public opinion or the judicial system.
Any natural satellite of a planet.
A moon or other smaller body orbiting a larger one.
One who brings messages.
A person who delivers messages.
to let go of

(also, reflexive, figurative) Often followed by from: to free (oneself or someone, or something) from some constraint or controlling influence (especially when evil or undue); also, to free (oneself or someone) from mental oppression.
The state of being stagnant; (countable) an instance of this.
A party or gathering held in the evening.
A formal evening party.
Greater than the speed of sound (in the same medium, and at the same temperature and pressure).
A subarctic zone of evergreen coniferous forests situated south of the tundras and north of the steppes in the Northern Hemisphere.
The external female genitalia of humans and other placental mammals, which includes the clitoris, labia, and vulval vestibule/vulvar opening.
An explicit set of requirements to be satisfied by a material, product, or service.
